primary_meaning: The end of the age / final judgment, when God reaps the earth, gathers the righteous (as wheat or grain) into his kingdom, and separates or destroys the wicked
primary_basis: Matthew 13:24-30, 36-43 (parable of the weeds: 'the harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are angels')
Revelation 14:14-20 (the harvest of the earth with the sickle of the Son of Man)
Joel 3:13 ('Put in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe')
Matthew 3:12 / Luke 3:17 (winnowing and burning of chaff)

alternatives.meaning: The present mission field / ready souls awaiting evangelism and gathering into the church
basis: Matthew 9:37-38 / Luke 10:2 ('The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few')
John 4:35 ('the fields are white for harvest')

alternatives.meaning: The reaping of moral or spiritual consequences / fruit of one's deeds or ministry
basis: Galatians 6:7-9 ('whatever one sows, that will he also reap')

alternatives.meaning: God's material or spiritual provision and blessing (abundance as sign of divine favor)
basis: Old Testament harvest festivals and promises (e.g., Deuteronomy 16; Psalm 67:6)

notes: The eschatological-judgment sense is the most consistently emphasized symbolic reading in biblical studies and historic Christian teaching when 'harvest' functions as a metaphor; contextual uses for evangelism and moral reaping are also frequent but secondary or complementary rather than competing primaries. No single meaning is exclusive; usage is context-dependent across OT and NT.
